events.text:
🇷🇺🛢 Russian Oil Fetches Premium Prices as Gulf Supplies Tighten
China and India are on track to buy record volumes of Russian crude in 2026, and some refiners paid a premium to secure it. With oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz disrupted, buyers who once counted on a discount for Russian barrels found themselves bidding against each other for cargoes that could reach their ports.
On August 17, Russia’s Urals crude was priced $3.20 a barrel below the Brent benchmark for delivery to India’s west coast. By September 14, it was $1.05 above, according to Platts. That same day, Urals still traded at a discount of nearly $22 at Russia’s Baltic port of Primorsk. The premium showed what Indian refiners would pay to get oil to their door. The price at the Russian dock told a different story.
In China, the bidding went higher. In September, sellers were asking more than $20 above Brent for November deliveries of ESPO, the Russian crude shipped from the Pacific coast, to Shandong province. A tanker loading in Russia’s Far East can reach a Chinese refinery without passing through Hormuz. When Gulf shipments became unreliable, that route gave Russian suppliers room to ask for more.
Chinese customs figures show how far refiners changed their buying habits. China’s total crude imports fell 15% in the first ten months of the year, yet its purchases from Russia rose 17%. Russia supplied roughly one in four barrels China imported. In India, Russian crude accounted for 38% of imports over the same period.
Russia had extra crude to sell because drone strikes and repairs forced some of its refineries to cut back. Oil those plants would normally turn into diesel and other fuels went overseas as crude. Temporary US sanctions waivers also gave Asian buyers access to more tankers and suppliers as Washington sought to keep oil flowing.
Russia’s pricing power now depends in part on how much Gulf oil makes it back to market. Indian refiners expect to scale back their Russian purchases if Middle Eastern deliveries return to normal. Until then, a Russian supplier with a cargo ready to ship can ask a higher price from a refinery that needs to know when its next tanker will arrive.

👹 Netanyahu warned against obstructing Trump’s Gaza plan as Israel risks becoming a pariah
US presidential envoy Jared Kushner has urged Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to honor his Gaza ceasefire commitments, which have been stalled by Israel’s October elections.
Under the 15-point roadmap agreed with Hamas in July, Trump’s Board of Peace and the White House are pushing to implement several concrete measures, viewing the Netanyahu government’s reluctance as a major obstacle. These include:
➡️ deploying an International Stabilization Force (ISF) in Gaza
➡️ allowing construction materials to be brought in for its bases
➡️ permitting 4,000 Israeli-vetted Palestinian police recruits to train in Egypt and return to Gaza
➡️ allowing water and sanitation supplies, as well as mobile homes for displaced Palestinians, into the Gaza Strip
➡️ launching a pilot project for a Palestinian technocratic administration in southern Gaza.
Speaking to New York Magazine, Kushner warned Israel against making the wrong choices: “Israel could rise from the tragedy of October 7, be much more secure and much more integrated into the world, or they can go on the current trajectory, which is to trend toward global-pariah status.” Axios reports growing frustration with Netanyahu among Trump officials, who see him as putting his political survival [ahead of the peace process.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/78247)
In the aftermath of the October 27 elections, Netanyahu’s coalition failed to retain its majority. The Likud party’s attempts to blame the setback on an alleged Arab conspiracy[ failed to gain traction.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77860)
Netanyahu’s political rival, Gadi Eisenkot, has already been tasked with forming a government. If successful, he could replace Netanyahu as early as next week. Eisenkot previously pledged to implement Trump’s Gaza plan within 18 months.

events.text:
🇾🇪⚔️🇸🇦 Yemen war escalates as Houthis step up retaliatory strikes on Saudi capital
Saudi Arabia and Yemen exchanged strikes on November 26, as the Houthis reportedly extended their attacks to Riyadh later in the day. The move marks a further escalation following a recent drone strike on the kingdom’s Public Investment Fund tower.
👉 Ansar Allah struck Saudi Arabia’s Jazan refinery earlier in the day, according to Major General Turki Al-Maliki, spokesperson for the pro-Saudi forces.
The coalition also claimed to have intercepted two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis toward the Saudi capital overnight on November 25-26, while an AFP journalist and local residents reported hearing an explosion.
Pro-Saudi forces also announced strikes on Yemen’s Hodeidah, claiming to have targeted a ballistic missile launch platform that had reportedly been used in the attack on Jazan.
👉 Meanwhile,Yemen’s Saba news agency reported that Hodeidah came under a series of Saudi airstrikes on Thursday. Saudi warplanes struck the Al-Qanawis district and a sewage treatment plant in Al-Mina district. The strikes reportedly put the facility out of service and wounded more than a dozen Yemeni civilians.
Located on the Red Sea coast, Hodeidah has repeatedly come under attack during the standoff between Yemen and Saudi Arabia. The city has remained under Houthi control since 2021 and serves as a vital hub for commercial imports and humanitarian aid.
Saudi fighter jets also struck Sanaa, the Yemeni capital, and the Sahar district in Saada province that same day.
Meanwhile, Press TV’s X account reported later in the day that Ansar Allah had launched an attack targeting Riyadh in retaliation for the strikes on Hodeidah and Sahar.
